jsesh.mdc.interfaces
Interface MDCBuilder

All Known Implementing Classes:
HieroglyphicTextBuilder, MDCBuilderAdapter, MDCModelBuilder, PrintMDCBuilder
public interface MDCBuilder

An abstract builder used to build the components of a MDC Result.

To implement a MDCBuilder, you need a) to write all method and b) you obviously need to implement some of the interfaces. It doesn't mean that the final result of your work should have a structure that reflect these interfaces : you can simply use them as wrappers, if you like so. That's for example what we do in jsesh.mdc.implementation.PrintMDCBuilder.

The clean OO way for parsing is to build an abstract parse tree. However, it means that if you need another structure, you build a memory representation for your data twice. There are cases where you prefer a single pass compile. The problem is that then you need to make some casts, which is both unclean and cumbersome. If someone has a better solution, I'd be glad to hear from it.

This builder interface is admitedly pretty complex.

In a first version, only "build" methods where here, and the rest (add, setLeft) were in the interfaces. getting everything in the MDCBuilder has an advantage : if you don't want to implement one of the interface, you can simply return null. Now, if you are not interested in modifiers, for instance, having an add method in ModifierListInterface meant that you had to instanciate a ModifierListInterface class.

An important note on the parsing process : the parsing order is not always easy to guess. It may sometimes be interesting to build temporary data.

addCadratToBasicItemList

public void addCadratToBasicItemList(BasicItemListInterface l,
                                     CadratInterface c,
                                     int shading)
Parameters:
l - an BasicItemListInterface value
shading - an int value with the following meaning : It's the sum of the following codes :
  • 1 : means the top left part is shaded
  • 2 : means the top right part is shaded
  • 4 : means the bottom left part is shaded
  • 8 : means the bottom right part is shaded
So a full shading is 15

addModifierToModifierList

public void addModifierToModifierList(ModifierListInterface mods,
                                      java.lang.String name,
                                      java.lang.Integer value)
Adds a modifier to a list of modifier. In the Manuel, modifiers are more or less of the form "\XXX000" where XXX is a string (usually reduced to only one letter) and 000 is an optionnal Integer value. XXX is made of letters or "?" 000 is a positive integer. both are optionnal. if XXX is empty, it's the empty string. if 000 is not here, value is null

Parameters:
mods - a ModifierListInterface value
name - a String value.
value - an Integer value. null if the modifier has no integer part.

addStartHieroglyphicTextToTopItemList

public void addStartHieroglyphicTextToTopItemList(TopItemListInterface l)
This method is called when the Manuel de codage construct "+s" is met.

+s is used to toggle between latin text and hieroglyphic text. In most cases, you won't need to do anything about it, and most builders will ignore this construct (well, implement it as a no-operation method).

The method is provided simply in order to allow the programmer to have access to a complete and faithfull representation of the original text.

Parameters:
l -

buildCartouche

public CartoucheInterface buildCartouche(int type,
                                         int leftPart,
                                         BasicItemListInterface e,
                                         int rightPart)
builds a Cartouche.

Parameters:
type - an int code, which describes the kind of Cartouche built. codes are 'c', 'h', 's', 'f' :
  • c : cartouche
  • s : serekh
  • h : hout-sign
  • f : castle
leftPart - an int value which indicates how the first extremity of the cartouche should be drawn.
  • 0 : do not draw this extremity.
for cartouches and serekh 1 : begin 2 : end (2 being normally the decorated part)

for Hout signs :

  • 1 : no square
  • 2 : square in the lower part.
  • 3 : square in the upper part.
e - a BasicItemListInterface value, the cartouche's contents
rightPart - an int value, which indicates how the second extremity of the cartouche should be drawn. Codes have the same meaning as for leftPart.
Returns:
a CartoucheInterface value

buildHieroglyph

public HieroglyphInterface buildHieroglyph(boolean isGrammar,
                                           int type,
                                           java.lang.String code,
                                           ModifierListInterface m,
                                           int isEnd)
Build a sign in context from a glyph and all corresponding comments.

Parameters:
isGrammar - is true if the sign is part of a grammatical ending
type - is a constant which states which kind of sign we have : a true hieroglyph (MDCCODE) or another symbol like a FULLSHADE or a REDPOINT. The values for these codes are in the interface jsesh.mdc.lex.SymbolCodes
code - the string with the manuel de codage code for this sign.
m - a ModifierListInterface which corresponds to the list of modifiers for this sign.
isEnd - 1 if the sign is a word's end, 2 if it's a sentence end, else 0.
Returns:
a HieroglyphInterface value

for values.

setHieroglyphPosition

public void setHieroglyphPosition(HieroglyphInterface h,
                                  int x,
                                  int y,
                                  int scale)
Sets the hieroglyph position for absolute placement.

x,y is relative to the top left corner of the cadrat. the unit used for them is 1/1000 of the height of the A1 sign.

scale is given as a percentage of the natural size of the sign.

This is mostly meaningfull in "absolute groups", written with "&&". in other groups, it might be used for fine tuning of the sign's placement, but the semantics are not really clear.

Parameters:
h -
x - abscisse
y - ordinate
scale - scale in percentage
